title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Praxis Payments
topics: Security docs: SOC2, KMS, audit logs
summary: Follow-up check-in ahead of renewal. Customer is happy with current latency but needs additional capacity for Q3 regional expansion and wants EU region residency. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for cost and data residency, requested updated pricing for dedicated capacity + dedicated GPU pool, security paperwork, and a short pilot for EU region. Agreed next steps: send pricing + contract amendment draft, SOC2 + KMS details, and schedule benchmark run in staging (Redwood SE to run LLM perf test).
next_steps: Send updated Dedicated pricing and contract amendment (Maya) by 2026-04-03
Share SOC2 report + KMS integration guide (Liam) by 2026-04-04
Schedule EU-region pilot & benchmark window with Praxis infra (Liam/Maya) - target week of 2026-04-13
Procurement to review amendment and confirm timeline (Nina)
action_items: Maya: prepare dedicated capacity pricing options + 12/24 month term comparison - due 2026-04-03
Liam: package SOC2 docs, KMS/HSM integration notes, and run initial perf benchmark in staging (collect p95/p50, throughput metrics) - due 2026-04-07
Praxis (Aisha): provide staging endpoints and example traffic profile for benchmark by 2026-04-06
Nina: confirm procurement constraints (PO process, preferred contract language) - due 2026-04-08
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood, Liam our SE is here too. How are you all?
[00:08] Aisha: Good, thanks. Busy quarter, but we wanted to get ahead of renewal and the EU roll-out.
[00:15] Tom: Yup, main things - capacity ramp and region data residency, also lock in pricing.
[00:22] Maya: Great. Quick agenda - capacity options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), region availability and egress, security requirements, then next steps.
[00:30] Liam: I'll jump in on perf and ops, what's your current qps and p95?
[00:36] Aisha: Currently ~120 rps average for our conversational flows, bursts to 350 during peak. p95 is ~210ms for generation token response but end-to-end with our app it's closer to 480ms.
[00:48] Liam: Okay that matches what we saw in the last run; dedicated GPU pools will reduce tail latencies with consistent throughput. Also prefix/KV cache helps a lot for repeated sessions.
[00:58] Aisha: For Q3 we'll be adding EU customers so we need data residency there. We can't route EU traffic to US unless we have clear contractual controls.
[01:06] Maya: Understood. We have Hosted regions in eu-west and eu-central — and Redwood Dedicated can provision a dedicated pool in the EU region. Redwood Private is another option if you need a VPC or on-prem.
[01:18] Tom: Cost's a big factor. Can you show cost delta between hosted and dedicated for our profile? We don't necessarily need private unless compliance pushes it.
[01:26] Maya: Sure - I can send a pro forma. Quick rule of thumb: hosted is lowest up-front but variable per-token; dedicated has commit pricing and lower per-token unit economics at scale, and private adds platform fees.
[01:38] Nina: On procurement side, if we're doing dedicated we want a 12- vs 24-month comparison and any early termination terms. Also, can you handle EU data residency in the SOW?
[01:48] Maya: Yep — we'll include region-specific addendum in the contract amendment.
[01:53] Liam: From a technical standpoint, for the EU pilot we propose: stand up a dedicated pool in eu-west-1, run a 24-hour bench with realistic traffic from your staging, capture p50/p95, throughput, and token costs. We'll also test fallback routing — if eu capacity hits limit, we can failover to a lower-cap model or queued burst policy.
[02:13] Aisha: That sounds good. A couple security things — we'll need SOC2 evidence, KMS integration for key management, and audit logs with retention.
[02:22] Liam: We have SOC2 Type II; I'll share the report. KMS integration is supported for Redwood Private and Dedicated via customer-managed keys; for hosted we can provide envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in some plans. Audit logs and SSO/SAML are supported, with per-request tracing in Console.
[02:39] Tom: One item — we're using an in-house filter for pii, so we need to know the retention policy for request logs and how to purge.
[02:46] Maya: Logs retention is configurable; default retention is 90 days but we can reduce or set retention policies in the contract. Purge APIs exist; Liam we'll follow up on API docs.
[02:55] Liam: Yep, I'll send the guide. Also note that the KV cache doesn't persist user text for retention unless configured — good for compliance.
[03:04] Aisha: On benchmarking, how do you handle model variants? We sometimes need lower-cost quantized variants for bulk inference.
[03:11] Liam: We support quantized variants and can route by policy. For latency-sensitive paths you can pin a non-quantized model and for cheaper batch jobs use quantized versions. We'll show the model catalog for performance profiles.
[03:22] Tom: Any competitors we should be aware of? We've looked at Anthropic and also considered running an on-prem stack to avoid egress.
[03:29] Maya: Anthropic was mentioned; budget-wise Anthropic hosted pricing was higher in your traffic profile. On-prem is possible but comes with ops overhead.
[03:36] Aisha: For the pilot we want Redwood to run the perf tests but we'll supply traffic and a staging endpoint. Also want to verify p95 under sustained 400 rps load.
[03:46] Liam: We can do that. We'll set up a dedicated pool sized for that throughput and run a 6-hour soak test to measure tail latency and throughput drop-off.
[03:55] Nina: Procurement question - if we go 12 months with option to expand, can we do a PO with milestone-based payments?
[04:02] Maya: Typically yes, we can accommodate PO and milestone billing. I'll have our legal ops prepare an amendment with payment schedule options.
[04:11] Tom: Are there any known limitations for EU hardware availability or lead times for dedicated pools?
[04:18] Liam: In some peak times there's lead time for specific GPU types; we can provision with a compatible GPU family and then migrate if needed. We'll include an SLA for capacity procurement in the proposal.
[04:29] Aisha: Great. Can we get costed options: small (current), medium (+2x), large (+4x) capacity with EU region add-on and 12 vs 24 month term?
[04:38] Maya: Yes — small/med/large with committed throughput, burst policies, and region add-on. I'll send that by Friday.
[04:45] Liam: And I'll attach SOC2, KMS docs, the Console screenshots for audit log config, and a benchmark plan template.
[04:53] Aisha: One more — do you support encryption at rest with customer-managed HSM?
[04:58] Liam: Yes, HSM/KMS integration is supported for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we can integrate with your cloud KMS depending on plan. There might be slight differences in key rotation cadence.
[05:09] Tom: OK. Sounds good. Next steps recap?
[05:12] Maya: We'll send pricing + amendment (Maya), SOC2 + KMS guide + perf plan (Liam), you'll send staging endpoints and traffic profile (Aisha), procurement will review (Nina).
[05:22] Nina: We'll aim to review by end of next week.
[05:25] Maya: Perfect — target pilot week of 2026-04-13. We'll follow up in thread and schedule the bench slot. Thanks everyone.
[05:33] Aisha: Thanks.
[05:35] Tom: Thanks.
[05:36] Liam: Thanks all.
